title: Web APIs
body:
Two different things go by this name, and it's worth keeping them apart.

**APIs on the web** — third-party HTTP services your code fetches data from. This is the sense used when consuming someone's JSON feed with [[Fetch]]; whether you're allowed to read the response cross-origin is decided by [[CORS]].

**Browser Web APIs** — the interfaces the browser itself exposes to JavaScript, which are not part of the language: `fetch`, the [[DOM]], `localStorage`, geolocation, canvas, timers. This is the reason `setTimeout` works in a browser but isn't in the JavaScript spec, and why the same code can fail in [[Node.js]] — different host, different APIs.
